match.reason: The only bank point on diffusion is about the spread of culture in geography, which is a different idea from the movement of particles and water across a membrane in biology, so no bank point teaches this card.

draft.title: Diffusion and osmosis
card: the net movement of particles from a region of higher concentration to a region of lower concentration. It needs no energy from the cell.
the diffusion of water across a selectively permeable membrane. Water moves from a region of higher water concentration to a region of lower water concentration.
A solution with more dissolved solute has a lower water concentration. So water moves towards the side with more solute.
Movement continues until the concentrations are equal, or until something stops it. Particles still move at equilibrium, but there is no net change.
draft.remember: Both are passive, and both move things down a concentration gradient. Osmosis is just the water version.

opts: Water moves across a membrane to the side with more solute
Solute moves across a membrane to the side with less solute
Water moves across a membrane to the side with less solute
Water moves across a membrane using energy from the cell
a.why: Water moves from a higher to a lower water concentration, and the side with more solute has less water. So water moves towards more solute. Moving water to the side with less solute reverses this.
a.clue: More solute means a lower concentration of water.

b.q: A piece of potato is placed in a strong salt solution. Mass is measured after an hour. What is the likely result?
opts: Mass falls as water leaves the potato cells
Mass rises as water enters the potato cells
Mass falls as salt leaves the potato cells
Mass stays the same as no water crosses the membranes
b.why: The salt solution has more solute, so a lower water concentration than the potato cells. Water moves out of the cells by osmosis, so mass falls. Salt leaving the cells would not explain a mass loss here, because the question is about water movement across the membrane.
b.clue: Which side has the lower water concentration?

a.best: Water moves across a membrane to the side with more solute

b.best: Mass falls as water leaves the potato cells

problems.detail: The why gives a flawed reason for rejecting 'Mass falls as salt leaves the potato cells'. Salt leaving would in fact reduce mass. The option is wrong because the salt concentration is higher outside the cells, so any net salt movement would be inward, not outward. The why should say that instead of 'because the question is about water movement'.

check.summary: The card and both questions are correct, and each question has a single clear answer. The why for (b) gives a misleading reason for rejecting the salt option: salt would move into the cells, not out, and that is why the option is wrong.
